lesson.name: Learn The Center Game And Danish Gambit
lesson.description: Learn the key ideas and main lines of the Center Game and Danish Gambit.

{What's the best way to target the vulnerable e4-pawn?} 3... Qe7 {[%wrong
There's a better option. Try again and look for a way to target the e4-pawn.] 
[%hint Attack e4 with your queen.]} (3... dxc3 $5 {There's nothing wrong with
accepting the Danish Gambit. See if you can also find a strong move to target
the e4-pawn.}) (3... d5 $5 {This is reasonable, but there's an even stronger
move to attack e4. Try to find it.}) (3... Nf6 $2 4. e5 {The knight must move
and White will win back the pawn on d4. Try again and look for a stronger way
to attack e4.}) (3... c5 $2 4. Nf3 {It's better to attack the e4-pawn. How
should you do it?}) (3... Qh4 $2 4. Qxd4 {It's better to pin the e4-pawn with
your queen. How should you do it?}) 4. Bd3 {Good start! How should you take
advantage of the pin on the e4-pawn?} d5 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try
again and look for a way to target the e4-pawn.] [%hint Occupy the center and
attack e4.]} (4... Nf6 $2 5. Nf3 {White sacrifices a pawn to take advantage of
the lead in development. Try again and look for a stronger way to target the
e4-pawn.}) (4... f5 $2 5. e5 {White sacrifices a pawn to take advantage of the
exposed black king. Try to find a stronger move to attack e4.}) (4... dxc3 $2
5. Nxc3 {White recaptures and develops, while the queen will be vulnerable on
e7. Try again and look for a stronger counter-attacking move.}) 5. cxd4 {
Nice move! How should you keep a material advantage?} dxe4 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try again and look for a good capture.] [%hint Capture a pawn.]
Well played! White doesn't have enough compensation for the sacrificed pawn.} *

is only slightly better. Try again and look for a better attacking option.}) (

c4-bishop. Try to find it.}) (9... Be6 $2 10. Bxe6 {There's a stronger move to

stronger pawn move to start an attack. Try to find it.}) (10... Bd7 $5 {

to find it.}) (10... c5 $2 11. a3 {There's a much stronger pawn advance on the
queenside. Try to find a stronger pawn advance.}) *

{How did World Champion Carlsen win material?} 8... Bxc3 {[%wrong There's a
stronger move. Try again and look for a useful capture.] [%hint Remove a
defender of the e4-pawn.]} (8... Nxe4 $2 9. Nxe4 {White wins material. Try
again and look for a stronger capture.}) (8... Rxe4 $2 9. Nxe4 {White wins
material. Try again and look for a stronger capture.}) (8... d5 $2 9. exd5 {
It's better to win material instead of sacrificing anything. How should Black
win a pawn?}) 9. Bxc3 {Good start! What should you capture?} Rxe4 {[%wrong
There's a better option. Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint

without allowing White a dangerous attack. You can revisit Nepomniachtchi -
Carlsen, 2017 in the next challenge.} (9... Nxe4 $2 10. Bc4 {This is
reasonable, but there's a stronger capture. Try to find it.}) (9... d5 $2 10.
Bxf6 {White wins material. Try again and look for a strong capture.}) *

c2-pawn.]} (15... Na2+ $2 16. Kb1 {White wins the knight with a good position.
Try again and check the hint if you're stuck.}) (15... Nxc2 $2 16. Nxd5 {
White wins material with a good position. Try again and check the hint if
you're stuck.}) (15... Nc6 $2 16. Nxd5 {White wins material with a good
position. Try again and check the hint if you're stuck.}) (15... Na6 $2 16.
Bxa6 {White captures on d5 next and Black is in trouble. Try again and check
the hint if you're stuck.}) (15... a4 $5 {This is a reasonable move, but

and look for a good capture.] [%hint Recapture and open the a-file for your
rook.] Nice work! White's king is totally exposed. You can continue Carlsen's
attack in the next challenge.} (16... Qc6 $2 17. Bd3 {White keeps a winning
material advantage. Try again and look for a stronger attacking option.}) *

{How did Carlsen take advantage of the exposed white king?} 17... Ra1+ {
[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a useful check.] 
[%hint Force White's king off of the back rank.]} (17... Qc6 $5 {This is a
good choice, but Carlsen found a powerful check. What did he play?}) (17...
Qh6+ $2 {Black is doing well, but there's a much stronger check. Try to find
it.}) (17... Qd8 $5 {This is a good choice, but Carlsen found a powerful check.
What did he play?}) 18. Kd2 {Great choice! How should you continue the attack?}
Qxb2 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a good capture.] 
[%hint Capture a pawn and defend the a1-rook.]} (18... Rxd1+ $5 {This is a
good option, but Carlsen preferred another great capture. What was his idea?})
(18... Qd4+ $5 {This is a useful move, but Carlsen preferred a strong capture.
How did he do it?}) 19. Qxc7 {Nice work! What did Carlsen play to convince
Nepomniachtchi to resign?} Rxd1+ {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and
look for a good check.] [%hint Trade pieces to remove the last key defender
around the white king.]} (19... Qd4+ $5 {This is a great move, but Carlsen
preferred another winning check. What was his idea?}) 20. Kxd1 {White resigned
in Nepomniachtchi - Carlsen, 2017. How would you checkmate in two more moves?}
Qb1+ {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a way to force
checkmate.] [%hint Check on the back rank.]} (20... Qa1+ $5 {This is a great
move! Try to find an equally good check on the back rank to force checkmate.})
(20... Qxc2+ $2 21. Qxc2 {White wins material. Try again and look for a
stronger check.}) 21. Kd2 {Great job! Where's the mate?} Qe1# {[%wrong There's
a better move. Try again and look for a way to end the game.] [%hint Look at
your checks. Which one is mate?] What a finish! The white bishop and rook
never moved.} *
